summary: This article explains how live theater combines a script, a director, rehearsals, and a whole cast and crew, with sets, lighting, and sound, to tell a story in front of an audience.
introduce: Start a K-W-L chart on the board and ask students what they already Know and what they Want to know about the topic of “Theater: Telling Stories on Stage”. Tell them they will fill in what they Learned after reading.

keyTerms.def: the written words and directions that actors use to perform a play
a practice session before the real performance
the person who guides actors and decides how a play will look and feel

challengeTerms.def: the group of people who watch a performance
the lights used on a stage to set the mood or show the time of day
a single showing of a play, dance, or other live event

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that watching a story performed live on stage is more exciting than watching the same story in a movie? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain the steps a group of people take, from writing a script to opening night, to create a live theater show.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review script, rehearsal, and director, and let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use audience, lighting, and performance in a short paragraph that connects the article to something they learned in another subject.
